issues.description: Unreachable break after raise; control-flow audit fails
issues.detail: The `break` statement immediately follows `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` inside the loop body. This is dead code — a raised exception unwinds the stack and the break is never executed. A careful reader would flag this as evidence the author did not trace the control flow. Either remove the break or restructure so the loop collects all misalignments before raising.

issues.description: Raising PerformanceWarning as an exception is a category error
issues.detail: PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass; the idiom is `warnings.warn(...)`, not `raise`. Raising it aborts the write entirely, which contradicts the docstring's claim of a "performance warning" and the PR description's question about whether an exception is appropriate. The test asserts `pytest.raises`, locking in semantics that are likely wrong. Decide: warn-and-proceed, or rename to a hard error like ValueError.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size computation uses wrong factor; invariant unstated
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` multiplies element count by itemsize to get bytes — fine — but `max(1, itemsize)` masks a zero-itemsize bug rather than asserting the invariant `itemsize >= 1`. Also np.prod on a tuple of Python ints returns a numpy scalar; the f-string interpolation will render as `np.int64(...)` in some versions. Use `math.prod` and assert itemsize.

issues.description: Loop invariant for divisibility check is not stated and only inspects dw[0]
issues.detail: The audit examines only the first chunk size `dw[0]` per axis, implicitly assuming `auto_chunks` returns uniform chunk tuples. That assumption holds in common cases but is not stated, and `normalize_chunks` can return ragged tails. State the invariant in a comment: "all interior chunks are equal; only dw[0] need be checked because the remainder is shape % dw[0]." Or check every element.

issues.description: Operator precedence ambiguity in `not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0`
issues.detail: Python parses this as `not ((nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw) == 0)`, which is what the author wants, but the expression is hostile to a reader. Prefer `if nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0:`. This is exactly the kind of opaque construct literate programming exists to prevent — the reader should not have to consult an operator-precedence table to follow a correctness check.

issues.description: Test name and assertion semantics drifted from intent
issues.detail: `test_zarr_risky_shards_warns` asserts `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...)`. The name says "warns" but the test requires an exception. Either rename to `test_zarr_risky_shards_raises` or switch the implementation to `warnings.warn` and use `pytest.warns`. Test names are part of the literate record of intent.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The algorithmic intent — rechunk to an integer multiple of the shard shape via `previous_chunks` — is sound and the parametrized test over region modes is a genuine improvement. But the misalignment-detection block has three rigor failures: dead code (`break` after `raise`), a category error (raising a Warning subclass as an exception when the docstring and PR description call it a "warning"), and an unstated loop invariant about uniform chunk sizes. The safe_chunk_size formula also leans on `max(1, itemsize)` to paper over an invariant that should be asserted. Tighten the control flow, decide warn-vs-raise deliberately, and state the invariant in a comment a reader can follow without running the code.
